translations.text: The book of the words of Tobit, [son] of Tobiel, son of Ananiel, son of Gabael, son of Anavel, of the kindred of Aser, of the tribe of Naphtali,
who was taken captive in the days of Enemessar, king of Assyria, from Thisbe, which is to the right of Kedesh, which belongs to Naphtali, in Galilee, above Aser.

I, Tobit, walked in the ways of truth and of righteousness all the days of my life. I did many acts of mercy and good deeds for my brothers and my kindred who went with me when we went to the land of the Assyrians, to Nineveh.

When I was in my own land, the land of Israel, in my youth, the whole tribe of Naphtali my father broke away from the house of David, from Jerusalem, which had been chosen out of all the tribes of Israel as the place where all the tribes should offer sacrifice. There he consecrated the temple of the dwelling of the Most High and built it for all generations forever.

For all the tribes that had broken away together, and the house of Naphtali my father, sacrificed in Dan to the golden calf that Jeroboam, king of Israel, had made, and on the high places of all the mountains of Galilee.

I alone went to Jerusalem many times for the feasts, as it is written for all Israel by an everlasting command. I went with the first fruits, the tithes of the produce and the first shearings of the sheep, and I gave them to the priests, the sons of Aaron, at the altar.
I gave the tithe of all the produce to the sons of Levi who served in Jerusalem.
I sold the second tithe, and each year I went and spent it in Jerusalem.
The third tithe I gave to those to whom it was due, as Deborah, my father's mother, had commanded me, because my father had left me an orphan.
When I became a man, I took Anna as my wife from my father's kindred, and she bore me Tobias.
When I was taken captive to Nineveh, all my brothers and those of my kindred ate the bread of the gentiles.
But I kept my soul from eating it,
because I remembered God with all my heart.
God gave me grace and favor before King Enemessar, and I was his buyer.
I used to go to Media. In Rages of Media I left ten talents of silver (that is, ten kankars) in trust with Gabael, the brother of Gabrias.
When Enemessar died, his son Sennacherib reigned in his place. The roads were unsafe in his reign, and I no longer dared to go to Media.
In the days of Enemessar I did many acts of mercy for my brothers.
I gave my bread to the hungry and clothing to the naked. If I saw anyone of our kindred anywhere who had died and been thrown out behind the wall of Nineveh, I buried them.
When King Sennacherib came back in flight from Judea, I secretly buried all those he killed, for in his anger he slaughtered many. The king searched for their bodies and did not find them.
Then a certain Ninevite went and told the king about me, that I was the one burying those dead. I hid, because I realized that they were looking for me to kill me. I was afraid and fled.
They seized all my property, and I was left with nothing except my wife Anna and my son Tobias.

Fifty days had not yet passed when his two sons killed him. They fled and went off toward the mountains of Ararat. His son Sacherdon reigned in his place. He appointed Ahikar son of Anael, my nephew, over all the chosen men of his kingdom and over all his administration.

Ahikar interceded with the king for me, and I came to Nineveh. For Ahikar was cupbearer, keeper of the seal, administrator, spokesman, and scribe of the chancery. Sacherdonsor [?] had appointed him second after himself. He was my nephew.
When I came to my home, my wife Anna and my son Tobias were given back to me. It was their feast of Pentecost, which is the holy feast of the seven weeks. They set my meal before me.
I sat down to eat and saw many dishes of food. I said to my son: "Go and bring back anyone you find among our brethren who is in need and who remembers the Lord. Look, I will wait for you."
He came back and said to me: "Father, one of our people has been strangled and thrown down in the marketplace."
Before I had eaten anything, I got up, took him up and carried him into a house until the sun set.
Then I returned, washed, and ate my bread in sorrow.
I remembered the prophecy of Amos, when he said: "Your feasts shall be turned into mourning, and all your joys into lamentation."
When I remembered this, I wept. When the sun had set, I went and buried him.
My neighbours reproached me and said: "He is no longer afraid of being killed! He had to flee because of this very thing, and here he is burying the dead again."
That same night I buried him. Then I came back, defiled, and lay down by the wall of the courtyard with my face uncovered.

I did not know that there were sparrows on the wall, and my eyes were open. The sparrows' warm droppings fell into my eyes, and white films formed over my eyes. I went to physicians, but they did not help me. Ahikar supported me until he went away to Elymais.
My wife Anna earned money by women's work. She would send the work to her masters and receive wages.
In the seventh month, [?] (the month name is unclear), she cut off the woven cloth and sent it to her masters. They paid her the wages and gave her a young goat as well.

When she came in to me, the young goat began to bleat. I said to her: "Where did you get this young goat? Is it stolen? Give it back to its owners, whoever they are, for it is not right to eat what is stolen."

But she said: "They gave it to me as a gift on top of the wages." I did not believe her. I kept telling her to give it back to its owners, and I was angry with her. She answered me: "Where are your acts of charity and your righteous deeds? See, now everything about you has come to light."
I was grieved and wept, and I prayed in anguish, saying:
"You are righteous, O Lord. All your works and all your ways are mercy and truth, and you judge with righteous and true judgment forever.
Remember me and look upon me. Do not take vengeance for my sins and for the ignorance of my fathers, who sinned before you.
For they did not obey your commandments, and you handed us over to plunder, captivity and death, and made us a byword and a reproach among all the nations where we are scattered."
And now all your judgments are true, in dealing with me for my sins, for we did not keep your commandments, for we did not walk in truth before you.

And now, according to the goodness of your will, deal with me before you, and command my spirit to be taken, so that I may be released and become earth; for it is better for me to die than to live, for I have heard false reproaches, and great grief is upon me. Command my release from this distress, now, to the eternal place, and do not turn your face away from me, O Lord.
On that same day it befell Sarah, the daughter of Raguel, in Ecbatana of Media, to be reproached by her father's maidservants.

For she had been given to seven husbands, and Asmodeus, the evil demon, killed them before they could go in to her, as is the custom with wives. And they said to her: "Do you not know that you strangle [?] your husbands? For you have had seven husbands, and you have not been named as wife of even one of them.
Why then do you torment us? If they have died, go with them yourself; may we never see a son or daughter of yours forever."

When she heard this, she was so deeply grieved that she meant to strangle herself, and she said: "I am my father's only child; if I do this, it will be a reproach to him, and I will bring his old age down with sorrow to Hades."
And she prayed to the Lord at the window and said: "Blessed are you, O Lord my God, and blessed is your holy and honored name forever; may all your works bless you forever.
And now, O Lord, my eyes and my face are turned toward you.
I have asked for my release from the earth, so that I may no longer hear reproach.
You know that I am pure of all sin and of man.

And I have not defiled my name, nor the name of my father, in this land of my captivity. I am my father's only child, and he has no other child to be his heir. Nor is there a near kinsman, nor a brother's son, for whom I should keep myself as a wife. Behold, already seven husbands have perished for me. From now on, what is my life for? If it does not please you to kill me, command that you look upon me, and have mercy on me, so that I may no longer hear reproach."
And the prayers of both of them were heard before God.

And the angel Raphael was sent to heal them both: to remove the white films from Tobit's eyes; to give Sarah, the daughter of Raguel, to Tobias, the son of Tobit, as his wife; and to bind Asmodeus, the evil demon, because it fell to Tobias by lot to inherit her. At that very moment Tobit returned and went into his house, and Sarah, the daughter of Raguel, came down from her upper room.
At that time Tobit remembered the silver that he had given in trust to Gabael at Rages of Media.
And he said in his heart: "I have asked for death; why do I not call my son Tobias, so that I may tell him about it before my death?"
And he called him and said: "My child, when I die, bury me, and do not neglect your mother. Honor her all the days of your life, do what pleases her, and do not grieve her.
Remember, my child, that she endured many hardships for you while you were in her womb; and when she dies, bury her also with me in one grave,
My child, remember the Lord our God all your days, and do not choose to sin or to break his commandments. Do righteousness all the days of your life, and do not walk in the ways of falsehood.
For when you do the truth, your works will prosper,

and so will the works of all who do righteousness. Give alms from your produce, and do not let your eye be grudging when you give your alms. Do not turn your face away from any poor person, and the face of God will not be turned away from you.
Give alms in proportion to what you have: if you have much, give alms from it in proportion to your abundance. If you have little, give in proportion to that little. Do not be afraid to give alms,
for you will be storing up a good treasure for yourself for the day of distress.
For almsgiving delivers from death and does not let a person go into darkness.
Almsgiving is a good gift before the Most High for all who give it.

Child, guard yourself against all fornication. First of all, take a wife from the family of your fathers. Do not marry a foreign woman who is not from the tribe of your fathers, for we are the sons of the prophets: of Noah, of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob. Remember our fathers from of old, my child: all of them took wives from among their own kinsmen and were blessed in their children, and their descendants will inherit the land.

And now, child, love your kinsmen. Do not let your heart be proud toward your kinsmen and toward the sons and daughters of your people, so that you refuse to take a wife for yourself from among them. For pride brings ruin and much turmoil, and idleness brings loss and great want, because idleness is the mother of famine.

Do not hold back the wages of anyone who works for you, but pay him at once. If you serve the Lord, you will be repaid with good. Be careful, my child, in all your works, and be disciplined in all your conduct.
Do to no one else what you hate. Do not drink wine to drunkenness, and do not let drunkenness go with you on any of your ways.
Give some of your bread to the hungry and some of your clothing to the naked. Give alms from all your surplus, and do not let your eye be grudging when you give alms.
Pour out your bread on the grave of the righteous, but do not give it to sinners.
Seek advice from everyone who is wise, and do not despise any useful advice.

At all times bless your Lord and ask him that all your ways may prosper and that all your places and plans may succeed. For all the gentiles have counsel, but it is the Lord himself who gives every good thing, and he humbles whom he wills, as he wills. And now, child, remember my commandments, and do not let them be erased from your heart.
And now I make known to you that I have deposited ten talents of silver, that is, ten kikkars, with Gabael son of Gabrias, in Rages of Khuzhiketi.
Do not be afraid, child, because we have become poor. You have much, if you fear God, keep away from all sin, and do what is pleasing before him.
Tobias answered and said to him: "Father, I will do everything you command me."

"But as for the silver that you said was deposited with Gabael, how can I get it from him? For I do not know him, and he does not know me. What sign shall I give him so that he may recognize me, trust me and give me the silver? And I do not even know the way to Media."

Tobit answered him and said, "He gave me a written bond, and I came away. We divided that one document in two: I took one part, and I laid the other with the silver. It is now twenty-six years since I deposited the silver." And he gave him the bond. And he said to him, "Now, son, look for a trustworthy man who will come with you, and we will give him wages. Then go and bring back the silver while I am still alive."
So Tobias went out to look for a man who knew the way and would go with him to Media. And he found Raphael standing in front of him, and he did not know that he was an angel of God.

Tobias said to him, "Where are you from, young man?" He said, "From the sons of the people of Israel, one of your kinsmen. I have come here to work and to look for hired labour." Tobias said to him, "Do you know the way to Media?"

He said, "I know it very well, and I am familiar with all its roads. I have been to Media many times, and I stayed with Gabael, our kinsman, who lives in Rages of Media. Rages is a regular two days' journey from Ecbatana. Rages is in the mountains, and Ecbatana is in the middle of a plain."
Tobias said to him, "Wait for me here, young man, until I tell my father, for I need you to come with me, and I will give you your wages."
And he said, "Very well, I will wait for you, but do not be long."

Tobias went in and told his father Tobit. He said to him, "I have found a man from among our kinsmen who will go with me." And Tobit said to him, "Call him here to me so that I may find out what tribe he is from, and whether he is trustworthy enough to go with you."

Tobias went out and called him. He came in, and Tobit greeted him first. And the angel said, "Peace be upon you." Tobit said, "What peace is there for me? I am a lowly man, weak in my eyes, and I do not see the light of heaven. I hear a man's voice but cannot see him, for [?] I lie in darkness." The angel said to him, "Your healing is an easy thing for the Lord. Do not be afraid." Tobit said to him, "My son Tobias wishes to go to Media. Can you go with him? I will give you your wages." The angel said, "I can, for I have been to Media many times. I know its roads, I have travelled through all its plains, and I am familiar with all its mountains."
Tobit said to him, "What tribe are you from, and from what family, brother?"

But he said to him, "What do you want? Are you looking for a tribe and family, or for a hired man to go with your son?" Tobit said to him, "Brother, I truly wish to know your name and what family you are from."
And the angel said, "I am Azarias, son of Ananias, of the house of Sedem the great, one of your kinsmen."

And Tobit said to him: "You have come alive and well, brother. Do not be angry with me, for I wanted to know the truth about your family. And behold, you are my brother, from a good and gracious family. I knew Ananias and Nathanael, the two sons of Sedem the Great, for they used to go with me to Jerusalem and worship there with me. These men, my brothers, did not go astray in the error of the children of Israel. You are from a good root, brother. You have come in peace."
"And I will give you a daily wage, and your food will be the same as my son's."
"Go with my son, and afterwards I will add more to your wage." And the angel said to him: "Do not be afraid. I will go with your son, and we will go and come back in peace."

And Tobit called his son and said to him: "My child, get ready and go out with your brother. May God, who is in heaven, bring you there in peace and bring you back alive, and may his angel go with you." And they prepared provisions for the journey and set out to leave, and he kissed his father and his mother. And Tobit said to him: "Go, and return alive."
And his mother wept. She said to Tobit: "Why have you sent this boy away? Is he not the staff of our hand? He goes out and comes in before us."
"Let no silver be added to silver. Let it be as refuse compared with my son."
"Let us live as life has been given to us by the Lord."
And Tobit said to her: "Do not be afraid. He will go alive and come back to us alive. Do not be afraid, sister!"
"A good angel will go with him. His journey will go well, and he will come back alive."
Then his mother stopped weeping.
And the boy and the angel went out and set off, and the dog went with them. They came as far as the river Tigris and stopped there to rest.
And the boy went down into the river to wash his face. A fish leapt at his feet, and the boy cried out.
And the angel said to him: "Grab it and catch it." The boy held the fish fast and brought it up onto dry land.
And the angel said to the boy: "Cut it open and take out the heart, the gall and the liver, and put them away carefully, for they are useful as medicine."
And the boy did so. They roasted the fish and ate it, and they kept the rest as food for the journey.
And the two of them went on and came as far as Khuzhiketi.
And Tobias said to the angel: "What kind of medicine are the heart, the liver and the gall?"
And he said to him: "The heart and the liver are for burning as incense before a person who is attacked by a demon or an evil spirit, and it will flee from him.
"And the gall is for anointing eyes that have white films on them. It is blown into them, and they are healed."
And they reached Ecbatana.

And the angel said to the boy: "We should rest today at Raguel's house, for that man is your kinsman. He has one daughter, who is very beautiful to look at, and it is right for her to inherit from her father.
"And it is right for you to take her as your wife, for she is more closely related to you than anyone else. She is strong and very sensible, and her father loves her."

And now listen to me: I will speak to him about her and ask for her for you today. And when we return from Rages, then we will hold her wedding. I know that Raguel cannot refuse you, because her kinship belongs to you more than to any other man. He knows that if he gives her to another husband, he is liable to death according to the law of the book of Moses. And we will bring her and take her to your father.

And Tobias said to the angel: I have heard about her, brother, that she has been given to husbands, and they were cut down in their bridal chamber at night when they went in to her. And I heard someone saying that a demon destroyed them.

And now I am afraid of that demon, because it loves her. It does her no harm, but if anyone wants to come near her, it kills him. I fear that I may die and bring my father's and my mother's old age down to the grave in grief. For I am [?] (probably "an only son"), and they have no other son or daughter to bury them when they die.

And the angel said to him: Do you not remember your father's command, when he told you to take a wife from the house of your fathers? And now do not be afraid, for I know that he will give her to you. Have no worry about that demon.
When you take her and go in to her in the bridal chamber, put the heart and the liver of the fish on the heat of the incense.

And tell her first to get up and stand on her feet. Then pray, both of you, and entreat the Lord, and he will give her healing. Healing and mercy will be upon you. And go in to her, and you will have children by her, for it is right for you to take her; she has been yours from eternity.

And when they came to Ecbatana and arrived at Raguel's house, they found him sitting before the gates of the courtyard. They greeted him, and he greeted them in return. And he said to them: Brothers, come in peace into the house of your brother.
And when they had entered the house, Raguel said to Edna his wife: How much this young man looks like Tobit, my brother!
Edna asked them and said: Who are you, brothers? And they said to her: From Nineveh, of the captives, of the sons of Naphtali.
Edna said to them: Do you know Tobit, our brother? And they said: We know him.
And she said: Is he alive? And Tobias told her: He is my father.
And Raguel stood up and kissed him. He wept and said: Blessed are you, child of a good and kind man. O what great evils, that a righteous man has gone blind
and he kept kissing him. And Edna his wife and Sarah his daughter wept, and they welcomed them warmly.
And they slaughtered a ram, washed themselves, and sat down to supper.
And Tobias said to Raphael the angel: Azariah, brother, speak to Raguel about his daughter, so that he will give her to me as my wife.
Raguel heard this and said to Tobias: Child, eat, drink, and be merry tonight. I know that it is not right to give my daughter to anyone else but you.
But I will tell you the truth, child: I have given her to seven husbands, and all of them died at night when they went in to her. And now eat and drink.

And Tobias said: "I will not eat or drink until you confirm the matter for me." And Raguel said: "What else can I do? She is to be given to you as your wife by the law, because you are her kinsman, as is right. May the Lord of heaven guide you both this night and grant you mercy and peace."

And he called her mother and told her to bring out a document. And he wrote a marriage contract, to give her to him as his wife according to the law of the book of Moses. And her mother brought it, and he wrote and sealed it
And only then did they eat and drink.
And Raguel said to Edna his wife: "Prepare another room and take our daughter in there."
And she did so. She took her into the bedchamber and embraced her tenderly. And she wept and said:
"Do not be afraid, daughter. May the God of heaven show mercy this night, look upon you, and give you joy in place of your former sorrow."
And when they had finished the joyful feast, they got up to go to bed, and they took Tobias into the bedchamber.
And Tobias remembered what Raphael had said. He took the heart and the liver of the fish and put them on the embers of the incense.
And the smell of the fish drove the demon away from the girl, and it departed. It fled to the upper regions of Egypt, and Raphael bound it there.
And Tobias said to Sarah: "Sister, get up and purify yourself. Let us pray and plead before the face of the Lord, so that he may grant us mercy and salvation this night."
And Tobias said: "Blessed are you, Lord, God of our fathers, and blessed is your holy name for all generations forever. May the heavens and all your creatures bless you.

You made the man Adam and gave him a wife as a helper like him, and from the two of them came the human race. And you said: 'It is not good for the man to be alone. Let us make him a helper like him.'

And now, Lord, you know that I am not taking this sister of mine out of lust, but in the righteousness of the law. Have mercy on us, Lord, on me and on her, so that we may grow old together in peace with each other. And give us children as a blessing
And together they said, "Amen."
And they slept together that night.
And Raguel told his servants to dig a grave during the night, saying: "If he has died, I will bury him at night, so that no one finds out and I am not mocked and laughed at."
And when the servants had gone out to dig the grave, Raguel called Edna his wife and said:
"Send one of the maidservants to the bedchamber to see whether they are safe and well."
And Edna sent a maidservant. She had a lamp in her hand. She opened the door of the bedchamber and saw that they were asleep together, safe and well.
She came out and told her. And she sent her to her husband and said: "They are safe and well."

And they blessed God and said: "Blessed are you, Lord, God of heaven and earth, with every blessing, perfect and holy. May all your angels and all your creatures bless you. May all your chosen ones bless you. May they bless you forever. You are the one who strikes and who heals.
Blessed are you, because you have made us glad. It did not happen to us as we expected; instead you have dealt with us according to your great mercy.
Blessed are you, who have blessed the two [?] and their parents. Grant them mercy and life, and bring their life to completion in mercy, with joy.
And the servants came, and he told them to fill in the grave before daybreak, so that no one would notice.
And he told Edna, his wife, to prepare a great feast, and she hurried [?] off. And he took two calves and four rams and ordered them to be prepared.
And he called Tobias, swore an oath to him and said: "You shall not leave my house until the fourteenth day, so that you may gladden the soul of my afflicted daughter.

Take half of my possessions at once and go in peace to your father. And the rest, whatever else there is, will be yours when my wife and I die. Do not be afraid, child; I am your father, and Edna is your mother."
Then Tobias called Raphael and said to him:
"Brother Azarias, take two camels and four servants from here and go to Rages, to Gabael. Give him this bond, receive the silver from him, and bring him with you to this wedding as well.
You know

that my father is counting the days, and if we delay and lose even a single day, my father will be distressed. And Raguel has sworn not to let me go for fourteen days, so that I would stay with them, and I cannot disregard his oath."

Then Raphael set out for Rages, and the servants with him, and they came to Gabael and stayed there. Raphael gave the bond to Gabael and received all the silver from him. He told him about Tobias, that he had taken Raguel's daughter as his wife and was there. And they invited him to the wedding as well. Gabael rose, brought out the bags, and showed him the seals. They counted the silver, loaded it on the camels, and set out early at dawn.

And they came together to Raguel's wedding and found Tobias sitting [?] at table. Tobias sprang up [?] and kissed Gabael, and he greeted Raphael too. And Gabael said: "Blessed is God, who has given you peace, for you are the son of a good, noble and generous man. Blessed are you, and your father and your mother; and blessed be your wife, and her father and her mother."
Meanwhile Tobit was counting the days from the day his son Tobias had set out. And when those days had passed, Tobit became distressed
and said: "Perhaps Gabael has died, and no one has given the silver to my son."
And Anna said: "My son has perished; he is no longer alive." And she lamented over him
and said: "Woe is me, child, light of my eyes! Why did I let you go away from me?"

But Tobit comforted her and said to her: "Do not be afraid, sister. Our son will come back alive; some hindrance has come upon him, and that is why he is delayed. Do not be distressed, for the man who went with him is trustworthy, one of our kinsmen. Do not let anything evil take hold of your heart."

And Anna said: "My child is lost to me." And she would go out and watch [?] the roads until sunset, to see whether her son was coming. Then she would go into her house, and she would not taste anything or sleep. And when the fourteen days of the wedding were completed, as Raguel had sworn, Tobias said to him: "Send me away. I know that my father and my mother are in distress, for they do not expect to see my face again."
And Raguel said: "I will send messengers to Tobit, your father, and let him know about you; but you stay with me for a few days."
And Tobias said to him: "Not at all, my father, I beg you; send me on my way, so that my father will not be grieved."

And Raguel got up and brought Sarah, his daughter, and gave her to Tobias. And he gave him a share of all his possessions: male and female servants, cattle and sheep, donkeys and camels, gold and silver, and a very great quantity of clothing.
And he sent them off. Raguel kissed them and said: "Go in health, children, and may the God of heaven prosper your way, and may I see your children before I die."

And he kissed Tobias and Sarah, his daughter, and said to her: "Daughter, honor your father-in-law and your mother-in-law, for from now on they are your father and mother, as we have been to you. Go in health, daughter." And Edna said to Tobias: "Before the Lord I give you my daughter, so that you will not grieve her all her days. And see, I am your mother and Sarah is your sister." And she kissed them both.

And Tobias went out and departed with joy, and he blessed God, the God of heaven and earth, and prayed, saying: "May it be granted to me to honor my father-in-law and my mother-in-law as my own father and mother all the days of their life."
And they went on their way and came to Caesarea, which is opposite Nineveh.
And Raphael said to Tobias: "You know how we left your father."
"Now let us hurry ahead and get the house ready, and let your wife come along at leisure after us."
And the two of them went on. And the dog ran ahead of them.
Raphael said to Tobias: "Take the fish's gall in your hand. And when you come near your father, he will come to you to kiss you, and his eyes will be open."
"Then smear that gall on his eyes, and the medicine will sting him and peel off the white film on them. And your father will regain his sight and see the light."
And Anna, his mother, was standing outside watching the road, and she saw the dog as it ran ahead of them.
And she ran inside and said to Tobit: "Look, your son is coming."

And Anna went out again to meet her son. And she embraced him and fell on his neck, and said: "Now that I have seen you, child, if I die now I will grieve no longer, for I have seen your face." And he came to Tobit.
Tobit was standing at the door, and when he heard his son's voice he wanted to go to meet him, and he stumbled about this way and that.

And Tobias ran to his father. And Tobit put his face forward to kiss his son, and both his eyes were [?], and Tobias poured the fish's gall into his eyes. And Tobit squeezed his eyes shut, because it stung him, and Tobit said: "Why have you done this, child?" And Tobias said: "Be patient, father, for it is a medicine of release."
And he applied it to his father. And the medicine peeled the white film off his eyes.
And he regained his sight and saw the light, and he blessed God. And he looked at his son and kissed him and said: "Now I have seen you, child."
"Blessed is the Lord, for I have seen my son. And look, I see my son. Blessed is the name of the Lord, the worker of wonders."

And Tobit and Anna his wife went into the house. They rejoiced and blessed God for everything that had been done for them. Tobias told his father how his journey had gone well: he had brought Sarah, the daughter of Raguel, as his wife, and he had brought the silver. "And look, she is near the gates, coming."

Tobit and Anna rejoiced and went out to meet their daughter-in-law, their son's wife. Their relatives and everyone who met them saw this and were amazed, because Tobit walked by himself with all his strength and no one led him by the hand. Tobit blessed God with a loud voice, for God had shown him mercy and opened his eyes.

When Tobit came near Sarah, his daughter-in-law, he blessed her and said to her: "Come in, daughter, for you have come safely. Blessed is God, who has brought you to me. Blessed is your father, and blessed is your mother, and blessed is Tobias my son, and may you be blessed, daughter."
And on that day there was great joy among all the Jews who were in Nineveh.
And Ahikar and Nabal, his brothers' sons, came to him and rejoiced with Tobit. And they held the wedding with great joy.
When they had finished the wedding, Tobit said to his son Tobias: "Let us give his wages to the man who went with you. And then let us add more on top of his wages."
Tobias said to his father: "Father, however much we give him as wages, it will not be hard for me, even if we give him half of everything that we brought back with us.
He protected me on the road and healed my wife. It is no loss to me, however much we give him."
But Tobit said: "It is right to give him half of everything that you had; and he came with you."
And he called the angel and said to him: "Take half of everything that you brought, since you have come back safely, as your wages, and go safely to your own place."

Then Raphael called the two of them aside and said to them: "Bless God and give him glory before all people for what he has done for you. Blessing God and exalting his name is good. Declare the words of God with honor.
It is good to keep a king's secret hidden, but the works of the Lord God should be declared. Do good honorably, and evil will not find you.
Prayer together with fasting is good, and almsgiving together with righteousness. Better than both of these is almsgiving; it is better than storing up gold.
For almsgiving rescues from death and cleanses from every sin. Whoever gives alms will be filled with life.
But those who commit sin and falsehood are enemies of their own life.
And now I will tell you the whole truth, and I will [?] hide a word from you.
When you prayed, you and Sarah your daughter-in-law, the prayers of both of you were heard before God. Your deeds were made known, and the acts of mercy that you did for the dead.
And when you got up from the table and wrapped the dead man in a shroud, and a trial came upon you,
then God sent me to heal you and Sarah your daughter-in-law.
I am Raphael, one of the seven holy angels who offer up the prayers of the saints and go in before the glory of the Holy One."
Both of them trembled and fell on their faces, because they were afraid.
And Raphael said to them: "Do not be afraid. Peace be with you. Bless God forever.
It was not by my own favour but by the will of our God, so bless him forever,
that I appeared to you all these days. I did not eat or drink; you saw only a vision.
So now give thanks to God, because I am going up to the Lord who sent me. Write down in a book everything that has happened to you."
When they stood up, they could no longer see him.
And they gave thanks for his great works and his wonders, and for how the angel of God had appeared to them.
And Tobit wrote a prayer of rejoicing for them and said: "Blessed is God, who lives forever, and his kingdom stands forever.
For he punishes and he shows mercy. He brings people down to hell and brings them up again. And no one can escape from his hand.
Give thanks to him, children of Israel, before the nations, because he has scattered you among them.
Show his greatness there. Exalt him before every living being, because he is our Lord and God, and he is our Father for all ages.
He punishes us for our sins, and he will again have mercy on us and gather us from all the nations among whom we have been scattered.

If you turn to him with all your heart and all your soul, to do what is true before him, then he will turn to you and will not turn his face away from you. And you will see what he will do for you. Give thanks to him with your whole mouth, bless the Lord of righteousness, and exalt the King of the ages. In this land of my captivity I give thanks to him, and I will make known the power of his riches. You sinful people, turn to him and do what is right before him. Who knows whether he will accept you and show you mercy?
I will exalt my God, and let my soul sing of the greatness of the King of heaven.
Let everyone speak, and give thanks to him in Jerusalem.
Jerusalem, city of the Holy One, he will punish you for the deeds of your children, and he will again have mercy on the children of the righteous.

Give thanks to the Lord well [?] and bless the King of the ages, so that his tabernacle may be built in you again with joy. Rejoice over the captives within you, and may he love the wretched within you for all generations forever.
Many nations will come for the sake of the name of the Lord God, bringing gifts in their hands, gifts for the King of heaven. Generation after generation will give joy.
Cursed are all who hate you. Blessed forever are all who love you.
Rejoice and be glad over the children of the righteous,
for blessed are those who love him, and they will rejoice in your peace after all their suffering.
And let my soul rejoice forever, blessing God, our great King.
For he will build Jerusalem with sapphire and emerald, its walls with precious stone, and its towers and battlements with pure gold.
And the streets of Jerusalem will be paved with ligure, carbuncle and stone from Ophir.
And in all its streets they will say "Alleluia." They will praise and say: "Blessed is the Lord, who is light for all forever."
And Tobit finished his prayer of thanksgiving.
He was fifty-six years old when he lost his sight, and after eight years he saw again. He did good works and grew more and more in the fear of the Lord God, and he praised him.
He grew very old. He called his son Tobias and his six grandsons and said to them: "Take your sons, for I stand at the point of departing this life.

Go to Media with the children. I believe that what the prophet Jonah said about Nineveh will come true: it will be destroyed [?]. But in Media there will be peace for some time. For our brothers will be scattered over all the earth, away from that good land. Jerusalem will be desolate, and the house of God that is in it will be burned and will lie desolate for some time.

Then God will again have mercy on them and bring them back to their land, and they will rebuild that house, but not as it was before, until the times of the ages are fulfilled. After this they will return from captivity and rebuild Jerusalem with honour. In it the house of God will be built, a glorious building for all the generations of eternity, as the prophets said about it.
All the Gentiles will truly turn and fear the Lord God. They will bury their idols in the earth, and all the nations will bless the Lord.
Their people will bless God, and the Lord will raise up his people. All who love the Lord God in truth and righteousness will rejoice, and they will show mercy to our brothers.
And now, my child, leave Nineveh, for what the prophet said will surely happen.

But you must keep the laws and the commandments. And you, my child, love mercy and be righteous, so that it may go well with you. Bury me and your mother properly, and do not stay in Nineveh any longer.

My child, remember what Adam did to Ahikar, who had raised him: how he brought him out of the light into darkness, and how the Lord repaid him. He rescued Ahikar, but he gave Adam what he deserved, and Adam went down into darkness. Manasses gave alms and was saved from the deadly snare that he had set for himself [?]. But Adam fell into the snare and perished.
And now, my child, see what mercy does and how righteousness saves." As he was saying this, his spirit left him on the bed. He was one hundred and fifty-six years old. They buried him with honour.
When his mother Anna died, he buried her beside his father. Then Tobias went with his wife Sarah and his sons to Ecbatana, to his father-in-law Raguel.
He lived to an honoured old age. He buried his father-in-law and mother-in-law with great honour, and he inherited their property and that of his father Tobit.
He died at the age of one hundred and twenty-seven in Ecbatana of Media.
Before he died he heard of the destruction of Nineveh, which Nebuchadnezzar and Ahasuerus took captive. He rejoiced until his death.
